title: Young, but Just Us: A Young Justice Retrospective (Transcripts)
author: SoleminiSanction
summary: "When comparing the 2010s-era Young Justice cartoon with the late 90s comic of the same name, it’s not unreasonable to start with the question, 'What do they have in common?' And, as someone who knows both, it’s tempting to say, simply, 'The name,' and leave it at that. The two stories are vastly different entities. But if you boil them down to their essence, the core difference between them is…surprisingly simple. Young Justice the cartoon is a coming-of-age story. It’s about growing up.Young Justice the comic is a being-of-age story. It’s about being young. And that makes all the difference."---An archive of the original scripts from my ongoing video project, a VERY in-depth retrospective and literary analysis of the 1998 Young Justice comic book series. Links to the videos and YouTube channel available inside.

The shorter man always looked exhausted, like he hadn't yet gone to bed, and the taller man was always bright-eyed and bushy-tailed like every other early riser she'd come across. It's late and Thad sits in a bar waiting for someone. And for no one else would he wait forever for.UPDATE:For more: I rewrote this entire fic and added around 7k more words and details as a new fic named: Here We Are Again Same Old Place***
  It’s late and the dingy bar at 2 in the morning slowed into a sleepy lull long ago, but Thad sits at the bar still with a fresh drink in his hand. For more than few hours he had waited right in that spot. It was uncharacteristic for some speedsters to sit still for so long. To go unmoving for so long without something else dragging him off, even for someone as patient as Thad, seemed unusual. He could have been anywhere in the world, or in any time period, but he had chosen this small dirty, dingy bar in Gotham. If anyone had come up to ask him as to why someone like him would choose to wait in such a place, a smirk would slide up the corner of his mouth, and such a rare light would twinkle would shine in his aged golden eyes.

title: Life After Life - Edited Version

tags: Tim Drake Does Not Get Help
summary:
Tim Drake has always been an excellent detective. Always been good at noticing things others don't. At picking up clues others miss. He solves mysteries. He has solved many, many mysteries, and crafted many plans to get him out of sticky situations. He figured out the identities of Batman and Robin, for goodness sake! So...
So when Tim wakes up in an abandoned warehouse surrounded by a pile of ashes and stains that he knows to be blood, with clothes stained in blood and a pain shooting through his entire body like nothing he has ever felt... the first thing he thinks to do is investigate. Search for clues as to what happened. And he will find out. Because Tim Drake is and has always been an excellent detective...
But what happens if the answer Tim finds is one that he will regret finding? What happens if the truth is too much for him to bear... and what happens if he finds himself in a situation he can't plan his way out of?

Superman doesn’t beg; not because he’s too proud or that he thinks he’s above it – Clark has simply never found a need for it and still hasn’t even now. He doesn’t beg. He doesn’t grovel. summary: Kon is supposed to be finding his passion, or following his dreams, or whatever it is that people are supposed to get to do when they don’t have to worry about working a job they hate just to make ends meet. He should be going to college, or traveling, or trying to find a job that he’d actually enjoy, or—something.But he isn’t.He can’t say why. Not really. He’s not really that introspective, he just knows that every reason he has to offer for not doing literally anything with his life tastes like an excuse, bitter and tacky and heavy with shame. Which, technically he’s not doing nothing—he’s still a Titan, still helps save the world on the regular, but… he’s been doing that for literally his entire life.Life is more than just superheroing. Kon’s team, Ma and Pa, the other Kents, and even various other capes had helped him learn that. He knows that he’s not a programmed machine, that he’s a person who gets to choose what he wants to make of himself.And yet…It’s just—He’s always so cold.

summary:
“You’re the Batman,” Clark said, trying to keep his voice warm, even. “I’ve heard about you.”
  Still no response. The wings shifted slightly, the sound low and dry, like wind moving through bone.
  Even folded, they loomed. Easily twelve, maybe fourteen feet in total wingspan. The joints flexed with subtle micromovements, like the Bat was resisting the urge to spring forward or flee. And the texture… rough, almost scaly, with no sign of feathers. All tendon and membrane. Like something prehistoric.
  Clark felt a shiver crawl down his spine.
  It wasn’t fear. Not exactly.
  “I’ve been looking for you,” he said, taking a cautious step forward, hands open at his sides. “Not you you, I mean. Others like me. Metas. People doing the right thing on their own terms.”
  No answer.
  “I thought you’d be taller,” he added, offering a small grin.
  Nothing. Not even a twitch.
  “Or… less grim.”

title: Breaking Vines
author: bblacknblue
summary:
In the gritty heart of Gotham City, where the streets reek of rain and ruin, Poison Ivy and Harley Quinn find themselves on separate paths after the collapse of their once fiery relationship.
Ivy, still nursing a broken heart, is struggling to move on while leaning on the quiet support of her close friends, Sam and Diana (see my other story, Scorched Hearts).
Meanwhile, Harley spirals—crashing on couches and bouncing through self-destructive flings.
Their worlds collide unexpectedly in a dingy Gotham coffee shop.
Harley, bruised in body and spirit, admits she’s been lost—desperate to feel something in a world that no longer makes sense without Ivy.
And Ivy, despite her guarded heart, still aches for the girl she once called home.
Their exchange is fragile, charged, and unresolved, but for the first time in a long time, there's a glimmer of something between them again—not forgiveness, not yet, but the echo of something that refuses to die.

title: Oh Darling, are we an Archetype?
author: That_One_Computer_Geek (T1CG)
warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary:
He was lying still on the metal table, his arms rested delicately along his sides like folded paper. Like someone had tried to make it look peaceful—make him look presentable. But Dick knew better. He knew that silence. That stillness. He’d seen too many bodies, too many ends.
  But not this one. Not his.
  “No,” Dick breathed. The word escaped like it had been punched from his gut. His head tilted to the side, slow and trembling, like his neck couldn’t hold the weight of what he was seeing.
  “No…”
  It came again, softer. Smaller. Like maybe if he whispered it, the universe would agree.
  But it didn’t.
  “No. No…” His voice cracked on the second one. Shook. His chest hitched as he took a shaky step forward. “No. No—no—”

summary:
Three weeks after Jon returns from his year-long trip with Jor-El, he decides to retire as Superboy.
He returns to the 21st century as one of the Lost Boys, the sensation of anti-gravity clinging to his frame like cellophane. Superboy fits like a too-tight shirt, sewn together by nostalgia and the fabric of childhood.
He is not quite a man, but he’s not quite a child. The things that he experienced have made him world-weary, more liable to look over his shoulder in the dark. He doesn’t dream anymore. When he does, his nightmares are filled with fire and magma and a sunless sky. He wakes with tears in his eyes and a jaw clenched so tight his teeth ache.
They thought he was dead. He guesses that's something to be thankful for, that when most people think of you as a distant memory instead of a real person, leaving behind the cape is easy. A quiet affair. A gentle mercy.In which Jonathan Kent reconsiders what heroism means, relearns how to fall in love, and returns to a home that he no longer recognizes.

summary: John didn’t ask for this. He didn’t sign up to be a hero, a savior, or whatever nonsense the universe seemed to have in mind. Time travel was complicated enough without stumbling across imprisoned magical deities. Yet, here he was—an unwilling do-gooder with a growing list of freed gods, spirits, and eldritch beings who now owed him favors.Not that John wanted their help. He just wanted a quiet life, free from divine drama and cosmic messes. But no, every time he turned around, there was another desperate deity locked up in some ancient relic or cursed dimension. He tried ignoring them. He really did. But then guilt—or perhaps sheer bad luck—always dragged him back.Now he’s neck-deep in magical debts, interdimensional grudges, and a timeline so tangled it could strangle a lesser man. The gods might call him a savior, but John knows the truth: he’s just tired. Tired of time travel. Tired of magic. And most of all, tired of being the universe’s go-to handyman.Someone, please, save him this time. Before he snaps and uses all those favors to take a permanent vacation in a timeline where none of this exists. If such a place even exists anymore.

La'gaan's chest rose and fell in a ragged rhythm as memories began to flood his system unabated. He had hoped his brain being in freefall would keep them away, but apparently today they just wanted to overtake him. He burst out of his chair, almost falling backwards over it. This was the last thing he needed right now. He almost turned and ran to the door, but a pair of hands gently grasped his cheeks, cool against his uncharacteristically heated skin and Miguel tilted his head down so their gazes were locked.
"Breathe querido." He whispered, demonstrating a slow, methodical breathing pattern. "Just like this."
He had no idea how long they stood there breathing together, but eventually La'gaans pulse slowed and M'gann slipped out of his mind. All of his focus was on Miguel and his concerned eyes, even if the world itself was still swirling around them. The Surfacer smiled, his hands dropping from La'gaans face only for La'gaan to catch one and put it right back, closing his eyes and leaning into the touch.

Bite your teeth down, dig your nails into his arms, just to keep from losing it entirely.Come for me, sweetheart, come for me, come. You’ve earned it.And, just because you are kind, because you are benevolent, you lean down to whisper in his ear:You can touch me, but only if you come. --Roy can be good, given the right incentive.(Title from Grief Lessons: Four Plays by Euripides by Anne Carson.)
